items.title: Carra: Lammens confidence worrying but Poch will feel Man Utd were robbed
items.excerpt: Jamie Carragher says Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens' confidence is a cause for concern after his howler cost Mauricio Pochettino a first win since taking charge.
body: Jamie Carragher says Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens' confidence is a cause for concern after his howler cost Mauricio Pochettino a first win since taking charge.
It was a nightmare performance for Lammens, who unnecessarily gave away the penalty for Luis Suarez's opener just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken first spot-kick.

Lammens, 24, then spilled a routine cross late in the second half which allowed Suarez to equalise for 2-2, denying United a first away win of the season and first away Champions League win for five years.

The Belgium international, signed from Club Brugge last summer, restored calm between the sticks last season after Andre Onana's calamitous spell as No 1, but has had a poor start to his second season at Old Trafford. items.title: Poch denied first Man Utd win by Lammens howler at Sporting
items.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.
body: Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.

United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half - the second courtesy of a divot on the pitch - only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.

Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.

United were also aggrieved by a decision to rule out a goal by Amad before the break for an alleged foul by Tielemans that resulted in the first of his two bookings. Sky Sports' Dan Khan described the decision as "genuinely one of the worst decisions I've seen live." items.title: Isak and Wirtz power Liverpool to easy victory at Club Brugge
items.excerpt: Liverpool recovered from their shock defeat to Fenerbahce in their last Champions League outing to beat Club Brugge 3-0 and improve their chances of a top-eight league phase finish.
body: Liverpool recovered from their shock defeat to Fenerbahce in their last Champions League outing to beat Club Brugge 3-0 and improve their chances of a top-eight league phase finish.

Andoni Iraola's side have had no problem scoring goals in Europe, but faced issues keeping them out. Brugge were most obliging hosts in that respect, a far cry from the regularly free-scoring side that have so far averaged 2.75 goals per game and beaten Inter Milan at the San Siro.

Felix Lemarechal was the home side's greatest threat. But Alexander Isak was far more decisive, netting the opener following Yann Sommer's misplaced pass before rounding off the scoring in the second half with a deft chip to beat the goalkeeper. Sandwiched between was a superb strike from the in-form Florian Wirtz, set up by a surging run from Rio Ngumoha.

Brugge got better, Lemarechal twice forced Alisson into saves and Nicolo Tresoldi, who has scored the same number of Champions League goals as Erling Haaland this term, also called the Brazilian into action. But Liverpool were creatively superior. Momentum is building. items.title: West Brom battle to win at Bolton
items.excerpt: Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre scored the goals as West Brom boosted their promotion push with a 3-1 Sky Bet Championship win at Bolton.
body: Norwegian duo Aune Heggebo and Felix Horn Myhre scored the goals as West Brom boosted their promotion push with a 3-1 Sky Bet Championship win at Bolton.
Hot-shot Heggebo gave James Morrison's in-form visitors a 21st-minute lead which was cancelled out by substitute Ruben Rodrigues' 63rd-minute penalty.
But West Brom, without injured top scorer Isaac Price, finished strongly, with Myhre's fifth goal since his summer move from Brann restoring Albion's lead after 75 minutes.
And Heggebo, back in the starting line-up after last Saturday's draw with Swansea, sealed a fifth win in eight unbeaten games with a penalty seven minutes from time.

items.title: Burnley break winless home record as Birmingham win at Turf Moor
items.excerpt: Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their Sky Bet Championship promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske's strike and Jaydon Banel's own goal.
body: Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their Sky Bet Championship promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske's strike and Jaydon Banel's own goal.

It is now 24 games since the Clarets last celebrated three points in front of their own fans, a nightmare run that has now stretched to 403 days. It represents the worst sequence in the history of English football.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, remain firmly ensconced in the drop zone. Coach Fabio Celestini has picked up just three points in the five games he has taken charge off since succeeding Nicky Hayen last month and his team were jeered off at the end.

For City, however, it was a timely return to form following the 1-0 defeat at Stoke on Saturday. This was a seventh win in nine for Chris Davies' team and they are just two places and two points off the automatic promotion spots.
